➡️ The change in the release time, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m., obviously attracts attention, and what is worth watching is the broader timing.

Sacks: If Dario Got His Way on AI Regulation, It Would Destroy Anthropic

@DavidSacks:

“There's a huge irony in the fact that Dario did not get his way in Washington for the most part.

Because I think if he had realized his dream of this highly regulated AI apparatus, I don't think (Anthropic) would be set up for a hugely successful IPO.

Why? Because their whole right to charge this massive premium for tokens is because they're six months ahead of those open models, and that six months would be eaten up in the blink of an eye if they were subject to regulatory approval.

Dario himself keeps writing these blog posts where he says, ‘We need an FAA for AI.’

“Forget about it. Your six months will be gone like that. Your model will be commoditized, the Chinese competitors will catch up, and that's bad for the United States, it's bad for our competitiveness, it's bad for the AI race.

But aside from just the geopolitical dimension, it'd be horrible for Anthropic as a company because, again, all their pricing power depends on them remaining in the lead.

If they ever slip up and lose that six months, they're toast.”

Jason:

“What does that do to revenue?”

Sacks:

“Exactly. A decent subset of the market is willing to pay a premium for true frontier intelligence. But Anthropic and OpenAI are on that hamster wheel. They have to stay in the lead in order to justify that premium.”

Did a lot of reading and thinking re: Where we go from here in the AI cycle over the weekend. 

On this website there exists a class of AI substack bros who have become very rich from being right on AI, and thus they have become the default signal for anything AI related. These guys bought Sandisk at $100, Neoclouds 50% cheaper, Bottlenecks before they ran up, and have YTDs of 10-20x. 

Given that SNDK was only at 200 at the start of this year, yea we had some magnificent gains. Now the next question to me is: Now What? Where will the next big trade come from?

My first instinct is that I am fitting a square peg into a round hole. These things tend to be obvious, and the fact that I have obsessed over this question over and over in the past few weeks is a red flag. AI was obvious at the start of the year, and hence it made money. So was crypto in 2024 when Trump got elected and we had a bull market.

But now, trying to "figure it out", is actually not a good sign. It's akin to trying to "buy crypto assets" in 2026 - you have to do so much logical convincing that these are good buys instead of facing the truth. 

And I can see it in my writing. I wrote to my subscribers a couple of days ago that these are just trading assets now. And yea the obvious easy bearish argument is that earnings are real, AI is real, and they will keep going up. I don't doubt that AI is real, earnings are real. But it's the consequence I doubt - that the prices of these assets can just keep going up ad infinitum when everyone knows that they are in need of compute and short of memory. 

My bread and butter have been asymmetric opportunities, which can be boiled down to one intuition - does it have good risk-reward? 

I think right now there's only 3 playing fields in the AI trade that offer good risk/reward

1. Buying microcaps that turn out to be strong competitors. 

2. Buying companies that become eventual monopolies / have a large stake, and aren't priced that way right now - Neoclouds are 

3. Buying new frontier-tech derived trades. Like if tomorrow someone says they want speed and CBRS just re-rates upwards 10x - that sort of trades.
